name: Quality of Life
author: neostryder
description:
Conveniences that faithful Angband does not have. Angband's own options belong to core, and this mod leaves them alone.

Enable it and you get the whole set, and each tweak has its own toggle you can switch off separately. Turn the mod off and the base game is exactly as it was.

rules.title: Auto-dig on walk
rules.description: Walking into a rubble pile or mineral vein you can tunnel through starts digging automatically, instead of just bumping into it. You still stop after each attempt and never step onto the dug-out square in the same move.

rules.title: Remember my settings
rules.description: Changes you make in the '=' options menu are kept, and every new character starts with them. Angband normally forgets them the moment a character dies, so every new life begins by setting them all again. Existing characters are never changed; each save keeps the options it was saved with.

rules.title: Keep reading a pref file past a mistake
rules.description: Angband stops reading a pref file at the first line it cannot understand, so one typo near the top silently throws away everything below it, such as a whole graphics pack or the rest of your keymaps. With this on, the whole file is read and the bad lines are skipped. You are told about the first 20 mistakes; any after that are skipped without a message, so they don't fill the message line.

rules.title: Remember cheat options too
rules.description: Include the cheat options in what is remembered, so a new character starts with the ones you had on. Off by default, because turning a cheat option on permanently bars that character from the high score list, and a new character should not inherit that unless you choose it. Needs "Remember my settings" to be on.

rules.title: Hover cards on the Map overview
rules.description: On the (M)ap overview screen, resting the mouse on a cell for two seconds (or holding for one second on touch) shows a card with a magnified tile and whatever you currently know about that cell: terrain, creature, item, trap, shop, or your own character. The card follows the same identify and memory rules as the main screen, so it reveals nothing early. Mouse cards close when the pointer leaves the grid; touch cards stay until you tap elsewhere. Clicking inside the map box inspects a cell instead of closing the overview, and any key still closes it.

rules.title: First-encounter alerts
rules.description: The first time this character meets a monster type, or picks up an artifact, a small card appears in the corner of the screen with its name and native depth. A monster's card also carries a threat badge - Unique, Deadly (well out of depth), Out of depth, or First sighting - so a dangerous or unusual monster stands out instead of scrolling past unnoticed. The card never takes the keyboard or blocks a click on the game underneath, and clears itself after a few seconds or on a click of its own close button. Tracked per character: a new character sees every card again.

rules.title: Zoom, pan, and responsive layout
rules.description: Use a responsive grid whose visible rows and columns change with zoom. Ctrl-= and Ctrl-- zoom, Ctrl-Arrows pan, Ctrl-Wheel zooms the area under the pointer, and two-finger pinch or swipe controls the map or play area. Hold Shift with a zoom key, or point at the sidebar while wheeling, to scale the sidebar separately. Only the game canvas pans. Display choices are shared by every character on this device.

rules.title: Sharpen zoomed graphics and Map overview
rules.description: Use crisp nearest-neighbour sampling for graphics tiles even when they are being reduced. This can make pixel-art edges clearer at zoom levels where the default high-quality downscale looks soft. It also shows every known dungeon grid on the (M)ap overview, smoothly reduced to fit in ASCII and graphics modes instead of using the classic compressed miniature.

rules.title: Itemize the quiver in the Inventory subwindow
rules.description: In the passive Inventory subwindow, list each distinct stack of ammo or thrown items in your quiver by name under a "--Quiver--" heading, as the quiver picker (the | command) does, instead of only a capacity count like "in Quiver: 7 missiles".

rules.title: Accessibility: enlarged display
rules.description: Use the responsive display at a larger, more readable default cell size. It works even if the separate Zoom, pan, and responsive layout rule is off, and does not change your saved normal zoom setting.

rules.title: Accessibility: high-contrast display
rules.description: Boost contrast and colour separation after the game has rendered each frame. It affects ASCII and graphics alike, including dungeon play, maps, menus, the Quality of Life status sidebar, and Map hover cards.

rules.title: Accessibility: colourblind correction
rules.description: Apply a red-green daltonization correction after the game has rendered each frame. It affects ASCII and graphics alike, including dungeon play, maps, menus, the Quality of Life status sidebar, and Map hover cards.

rules.title: Accessibility: activation shortcut helper
rules.description: When you learn a spell or gain a known activatable item, offer to bind the casting or activation command to an unused shortcut key. You can accept the suggested function key, choose a different key, or decline each offer.

rules.title: Accessibility: repeated-action shortcuts
rules.description: Offer unused one-key shortcuts for resting as needed and, in the original keyset, running in each cardinal direction. They start the game's ordinary rest or run command and never replace an existing shortcut.

rules.title: Purge queued input
rules.description: Claim an unused key (F2, if nothing else already has it) that sends Escape for you, enough presses at once to back out of several stacked menus or prompts instead of clearing them one Escape at a time. Holding the key down does not repeat the purge. The host decides whether a keypress is a new press or the key still being held, and only a new press purges, so an accidental long hold purges once rather than for as long as the key stays down. Separate presses in quick succession each purge again.

rules.title: Quality ignore: always ignore torches
rules.description: Treat every Wooden Torch as ignored, whatever quality tier you have set for light sources and whether or not the lantern toggle below is on. A torch artifact, or a torch inscribed !k or !*, is never ignored by this.

rules.title: Quality ignore: always ignore lanterns
rules.description: Treat every Lantern as ignored, whatever quality tier you have set for light sources and whether or not the torch toggle above is on. The two toggles are separate so you can ignore only torches, for example if you refuel a Lantern of Shadows from lanterns found on the ground. A lantern artifact, or a lantern inscribed !k or !*, is never ignored by this.

sections.title: Misc. niceties
sections.description: Bundle small independent conveniences that are not each worth a separate setting. It shows an ellipsis instead of silently cutting off a store item name that is too long for its column, shows the selected store item's full description on the message line while browsing, and adds a one-line colour key to the visible-monster list ('[') explaining that violet marks a unique and red marks a monster whose native level is above the current dungeon depth. It also makes clarity and wording improvements to upstream Angband's own text, in item and monster descriptions and in game messages. More independent niceties can join this switch later.
